plain: Prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa: what kappa would be if YES and NO were equally common and the judges equally keen on YES.
eli5: Kappa with the “almost everything is no” effect taken out.
technical: Byrt, Bishop and Carlin (1993): PABAK = 2p<sub>o</sub> − 1, with prevalence index PI = (a − d)/n and bias index BI = (b − c)/n; kappa is recovered exactly from the three.
